claim: A CloudWatch metric exists only in the Region in which it is created.
q: In which Region can you see a CloudWatch metric?
v: Metrics exist only in the Region in which they are created
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Metrics exist only in the Region in which they are created.

claim: CloudWatch has no default namespace, so you must specify a namespace for each data point you publish.
q: Does CloudWatch have a default namespace for custom metrics?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
There is no default namespace. You must specify a namespace for each data point you publish to CloudWatch.

claim: A namespace is a container for CloudWatch metrics; metrics in different namespaces are isolated from each other, so metrics from different applications are not aggregated into the same statistics by mistake.
q: What is a CloudWatch namespace for?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

A *namespace* is a container for CloudWatch metrics. Metrics in different namespaces are isolated from each other, so that metrics from different applications are not mistakenly aggregated into the same statistics.

claim: A metric is uniquely defined by a name, a namespace, and zero or more dimensions.
q: What uniquely identifies a CloudWatch metric?
v: uniquely defined by a name, a namespace
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Metrics are uniquely defined by a name, a namespace, and zero or more dimensions.

claim: A dimension is a name/value pair that is part of the identity of a metric, and CloudWatch treats each unique combination of dimensions as a separate metric even when the metric name is the same.
q: What is a CloudWatch dimension and how does it change a metric's identity?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
A *dimension* is a name/value pair that is part of the identity of a metric.
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
CloudWatch treats each unique combination of dimensions as a separate metric, even if the metrics have the same metric name.

claim: CloudWatch can aggregate data across dimensions for metrics from certain AWS services such as Amazon EC2, but it does not aggregate across dimensions for custom metrics.
q: Does CloudWatch aggregate across dimensions for custom metrics?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

For metrics produced by certain AWS services, such as Amazon EC2, CloudWatch can aggregate data across dimensions. For example, if you search for metrics in the `AWS/EC2` namespace but do not specify any dimensions, CloudWatch aggregates all data for the specified metric to create the statistic that you requested. CloudWatch does not aggregate across dimensions for your custom metrics.

claim: By default many AWS services provide metrics at no charge for resources such as Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon EBS volumes and Amazon RDS DB instances; for a charge you can enable detailed monitoring for some resources, such as EC2 instances, or publish your own application metrics.
q: Are the default metrics of AWS services free, and what costs extra?
v: For a charge, you can also enable detailed monitoring
cond: Detailed monitoring is available for some resources only.
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

By default, many AWS services provide metrics at no charge for resources (such as Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon EBS volumes, and Amazon RDS DB instances). For a charge, you can also enable detailed monitoring for some resources, such as your Amazon EC2 instances, or publish your own application metrics.

claim: Metrics produced by AWS services are standard resolution by default; when you publish a custom metric you can define it as either standard resolution or high resolution.
q: What resolution do AWS service metrics have, and what can you choose for a custom metric?
v: either standard resolution or high resolution
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Metrics produced by AWS services are standard resolution by default. When you publish a custom metric, you can define it as either standard resolution or high resolution.

claim: A high-resolution metric has data at a granularity of one second, while a standard-resolution metric has a one-minute granularity.
q: What granularity does a high-resolution CloudWatch metric have?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Standard resolution, with data having a one-minute granularity
docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
High resolution, with data at a granularity of one second

claim: Every PutMetricData call for a custom metric is charged, so calling PutMetricData more often on a high-resolution metric can lead to higher charges.
q: Why can high-resolution custom metrics cost more?
v: every PutMetricData call for a custom metric is charged
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Keep in mind that every `PutMetricData` call for a custom metric is charged, so calling `PutMetricData` more often on a high-resolution metric can lead to higher charges.

claim: For an alarm on a high-resolution metric you can specify a high-resolution alarm with a period of 10 seconds or 30 seconds, or a regular alarm with a period of any multiple of 60 seconds; high-resolution alarms with a period of 10 or 30 seconds cost more.
q: What alarm periods can you use on a high-resolution metric, and is there a price difference?
sc: per alarm on a high-resolution metric
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

If you set an alarm on a high-resolution metric, you can specify a high-resolution alarm with a period of 10 seconds or 30 seconds, or you can set a regular alarm with a period of any multiple of 60 seconds. There is a higher charge for high-resolution alarms with a period of 10 or 30 seconds.

claim: Only custom metrics that you define with a storage resolution of 1 second support sub-minute periods.
q: Which metrics support periods shorter than 60 seconds?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Only custom metrics that you define with a storage resolution of 1 second support sub-minute periods.

claim: For large datasets you can insert a pre-aggregated statistic set, in which you give CloudWatch the Min, Max, Sum, and SampleCount for a number of data points.
q: How can you send many data points to CloudWatch without publishing every one?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
For large datasets, you can insert a pre-aggregated dataset called a *statistic set*. With statistic sets, you give CloudWatch the Min, Max, Sum, and SampleCount for a number of data points.

claim: CloudWatch does not automatically aggregate data across Regions, but you can use metric math to aggregate metrics from different Regions.
q: Does CloudWatch aggregate metrics across Regions by itself?
v: does not automatically aggregate data across Regions
use metric math to aggregate metrics from different Regions
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
CloudWatch does not automatically aggregate data across Regions, but you can use metric math to aggregate metrics from different Regions.

claim: If you publish a metric with the same namespace and dimensions from different sources, CloudWatch treats it as a single metric.
q: What does CloudWatch do when many hosts publish a metric with the same namespace and dimensions?
v: treats this as a single metric
doesn't differentiate the source of a metric
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts
Amazon CloudWatch doesn't differentiate the source of a metric. If you publish a metric with the same namespace and dimensions from different sources, CloudWatch treats this as a single metric.

claim: Percentile statistics are not available for a metric when any of its values are negative numbers; for custom metrics they are available as long as you publish the raw, unsummarized data points.
q: When can you not use percentile statistics on a CloudWatch metric?
v: not available for metrics when any of the metric values are negative numbers
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

Percentile statistics are available for custom metrics as long as you publish the raw, unsummarized data points for your custom metric. Percentile statistics are not available for metrics when any of the metric values are negative numbers.

claim: CloudWatch alarms invoke actions only for sustained state changes: an alarm does not invoke actions simply because it is in a particular state; the state must have changed and been maintained for a specified number of periods.
q: Does a CloudWatch alarm run its actions every time it evaluates in the ALARM state?
v: do not invoke actions simply because they are in a particular state
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

Alarms invoke actions for sustained state changes only. CloudWatch alarms do not invoke actions simply because they are in a particular state. The state must have changed and been maintained for a specified number of periods.

claim: An alarm watches a single metric over a specified time period and performs one or more actions based on the metric's value relative to a threshold over time; the action is a notification sent to an Amazon SNS topic or an Auto Scaling policy.
q: What does a CloudWatch alarm watch and what actions does it take?
v: notification sent to an Amazon SNS topic or an Auto Scaling policy
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

An alarm watches a single metric over a specified time period, and performs one or more specified actions, based on the value of the metric relative to a threshold over time. The action is a notification sent to an Amazon SNS topic or an Auto Scaling policy.

claim: Choose an alarm period that is greater than or equal to the metric's resolution: basic monitoring for Amazon EC2 provides metrics every 5 minutes, so an alarm on such a metric needs a period of at least 300 seconds, while detailed monitoring provides a resolution of 1 minute.
q: What alarm period fits an EC2 basic monitoring metric, and what does detailed monitoring change?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

For example, basic monitoring for Amazon EC2 provides metrics for your instances every 5 minutes. When setting an alarm on a basic monitoring metric, select a period of at least 300 seconds (5 minutes). Detailed monitoring for Amazon EC2 provides metrics for your instances with a resolution of 1 minute.

claim: Custom metrics sent with time stamps other than the current UTC time can make alarms show the Insufficient Data state or cause delayed alarms, because CloudWatch alarms check metrics based on the current time in UTC.
q: Why can an alarm on a custom metric show Insufficient Data even though data is published?
ev: docs/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch_concepts

CloudWatch alarms check metrics based on the current time in UTC. Custom metrics sent to CloudWatch with time stamps other than the current UTC time can cause alarms to display the **Insufficient Data** state or result in delayed alarms.
